ask.title: Ask — Query your knowledge base
ask.summary: Ask questions about tickers, setups, and strategies in plain language and get cited answers from your sources.
ask.body:
Type any question — for example 'What are the channels saying about AAPL breakouts?' or 'What is the best-performing setup for tech stocks?'. The system retrieves relevant content from all ingested sources, synthesizes a bilingual answer, and shows the exact source evidence it used.

Answers respect your current display language. The more sources you have ingested, the richer and more specific the answers.

If the Ask view returns an error about the overage ceiling, your workspace's compute budget has been exhausted for this billing period — see Billing for details.

sources.title: Sources — Ingestion & content filters
sources.summary: Sources are the Telegram channels and YouTube channels your workspace ingests trading content from.
sources.body:
Telegram: first connect a Telegram account (you need an API ID and API Hash from my.telegram.org — this is your own developer credential, not a shared one). A workspace can have more than one connected account. Then add a channel by its handle or numeric ID, select which account to read it through, and choose a fetch cadence (real-time ≈1 min, hourly, or daily).

YouTube: add a channel by its handle (@name), channel ID (UCxxx…), or playlist ID. Requires YOUTUBE_API_KEY in server config. TradeMind prefers native captions; if none are available it falls back to Whisper transcription.

Content type filters (per source): uncheck image, video, or URL processing for channels where those types are never useful. Disabling them is the most direct way to reduce per-source cost — disabled types are skipped before any expensive processing runs.

Backfill: when you add a new source you can optionally pull historical content from a specific date forward. You can also trigger on-demand date-range backfills at any time from the source card. Backfill jobs show live status (queued / running / completed / failed).

library.title: Strategy Library — Discovered trading patterns
library.summary: The strategy library shows validated trading patterns that the system has mined from your connected sources.
library.body:
Each strategy card is generated by the pattern mining engine, which clusters similar trade ideas by symbol, setup type, and indicator combination across all sources.

A card shows: setup type, plain-language description in your chosen language, win rate with 95% confidence interval (once validated), a walk-forward check (flags potential overfitting), and a flowchart of how to trade the setup.

Click 'How to trade it' to open the full detail view — which also shows cited real examples from the original sources, an outcome breakdown (won/lost/open), and your personal execution history for that setup.

Confidence tiers reflect how much evidence backs a pattern:
• Still learning — few examples, treat as exploratory
• Developing — building evidence, some validation data
• Established — well-evidenced, consistent validation results

Use 'Run pattern mining' after ingesting new content to refresh cards. Mining runs automatically every Sunday.

plan.title: My Plan — Personal strategy curation
plan.summary: My Plan is your private shortlist of strategy cards you are actively watching or trading.
plan.body:
Add any strategy card to your plan from the Library or the card detail view. Each plan item has:
• Status: Watching (monitoring), Adopted (actively trading), or Rejected (not a fit)
• Personal notes: your observations, conditions, or reminders
• Risk tolerance match: Low / Medium / High — your own assessment of how well this setup fits your risk profile

Plan items are always private — they are scoped to you individually and never visible to other workspace members, even on a shared workspace.

Use 'View card' on any plan item to jump directly to the full strategy detail, including the flowchart, cited examples, and your personal execution history.

trading.title: Paper Trading — Practice execution
trading.summary: Paper trading lets you practice executing strategies without risking real money, using an Alpaca paper account.
trading.body:
Propose an order from a strategy card using the 'Propose paper order' button, or create one manually from the Paper Trading page. Orders follow a strict status flow:

1. Proposed — draft order, nothing sent anywhere
2. Confirmed — you explicitly confirmed it (mandatory step, can never be skipped)
3. Submitted — sent to Alpaca's paper trading API
4. Filled / Rejected / Cancelled — terminal states

The confirmation step is a hard gate — no order can be submitted without it. This ensures you always consciously review before any trade reaches Alpaca.

Once submitted, use 'Refresh status' to poll Alpaca for the current state. When an order fills, a journal entry is created automatically.

Close trades by recording an exit price on a journal entry. Then use 'Score my trades' to evaluate your execution against the strategy's predicted levels using real market data.

Requires ALPACA_API_KEY and ALPACA_SECRET_KEY in server config (your own Alpaca paper account credentials).

billing.title: Billing & Cost Dashboard
billing.summary: The Billing page shows your subscription plan, current period spend vs budget, overage, and a full cost breakdown by task type.
billing.body:
TradeMind tracks every LLM, transcription, vision, and embedding call with its exact cost. This data is shown in the cost breakdown table.

Budget behavior:
• Included budget: the compute allowance your plan covers. Once exhausted, background ingestion and pattern mining pause automatically — but the Ask view keeps working.
• Overage: spend beyond the included budget (from queries you make while the budget is exhausted) is metered and added to your next invoice at the overage rate (1.5× raw cost).
• Overage ceiling: a hard backstop — if reached, even query synthesis pauses until the next billing period or a plan upgrade.

To subscribe, click 'Subscribe'. You will be redirected to Stripe's secure hosted payment page — no card data ever passes through TradeMind's servers.

Use 'Manage billing' to update your payment method, view invoices, or cancel your subscription. Changes sync automatically via webhook.

Billing status changes (lapses, reactivations, overrides) are always visible to workspace members — there are no silent status changes.

changelog.title: Changelog — Learning loop activity
changelog.summary: The Changelog shows what changed in your strategy cards over time and why.
changelog.body:
Each time pattern mining or validation runs and a strategy card changes meaningfully, a version snapshot is recorded: what the win rate and confidence tier were before, what they became, and what drove the change.

Change sources:
• Mining: new or updated trade ideas changed the sample size, source diversity, or tier
• Validation: new market outcome data changed the win rate or tier

Use 'Recompute (mining + validation)' to manually trigger a fresh run across all cards for your workspace. This is useful after a large backfill or when you want to see updated stats immediately rather than waiting for the weekly scheduled run.

Card versions are never silently overwritten — the history is always preserved.

admin.title: Admin/Config — Workspace settings
admin.summary: The Admin view manages your workspace's platform connections, tracked channels, content filters, topic scope, and backfill settings.
admin.body:
Platform connections: connect Telegram accounts (each workspace can have more than one — useful for channels that require specific account membership or for spreading rate-limit load). YouTube sources use the YOUTUBE_API_KEY server config, no separate account needed.

Topic scope: the plain-language description of what counts as on-topic for your workspace (default: stock trading, equities, market analysis). The relevance filter checks every incoming item against this before running any expensive processing. Broaden it to include crypto/forex, or narrow it to a specific market — off-topic content is tagged and skipped from all downstream steps.

Content type filters: set per source. Disable image, video, or URL processing for sources where those types are never useful. Disabled types are skipped before any LLM or transcription call — the most direct cost lever available.

Backfill: pull historical content over a specific date range for any source. Jobs track their own status (queued / running / completed / failed) and report items ingested.

onboarding.step1Body: TradeMind ingests trading content from Telegram and YouTube channels, extracts structured trade ideas, mines recurring patterns, validates them against real market outcomes, and teaches them back to you — with evidence, not just signals.
onboarding.step2Body: Go to Sources to connect a Telegram account or add a YouTube channel. Once content is ingested, pattern mining will discover recurring setups across your sources.
onboarding.step3Body: Once you have content ingested, head to Ask and ask any question about tickers, setups, or strategies. Answers are cited back to the original source.
